target.title: feat: clarify iOS Location Always permission flow
target.body:
Related: #99229
Related: #86217
Related closed candidate: #99235

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where iOS users could select Location Always in OpenClaw without the app clearly explaining whether iOS had actually granted background-capable location access. That made wake-up/location workflows ambiguous when iOS only allowed While Using, denied access, global Location Services were disabled, or the user changed OpenClaw/iOS location settings independently.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an explicit iOS permission summary for Location settings that separates the user's selected OpenClaw mode from the effective iOS authorization state. It also wires the background-location contract into the native configuration and location service path: background updates are only enabled for Always-capable use, significant-change monitoring is stopped when the mode is disabled, downgraded, or no longer authorized Always, and app-level Location Off remains a sticky OpenClaw preference even when iOS still grants permission.

This follows the current SettingsProTab pattern for now because #99231 may reshape the Settings UI.

#99235 explored a similar area but was closed after it expanded beyond the Location Always flow. This PR keeps the scope narrower: Location permission copy, native i18n inventory, Info.plist background location declaration, background/significant-change monitoring gates, and focused tests.

## User Impact

Users get clearer feedback when Location Always is selected but iOS has not granted background-capable permission. Operators and reviewers also get a cleaner contract for when the iOS app may use background location behavior.

Use cases covered:

- Keep OpenClaw reachable for location-triggered/background wake-up workflows when the user explicitly selects Always and iOS grants Always.
- Show a warning when Always is selected but iOS only grants While Using, so users understand background location will not work.
- Preserve the selected Always mode in that mismatch state instead of reverting to the previous app setting.
- Show a warning when location is denied, restricted, or globally disabled in iOS settings.
- Preserve OpenClaw Location Off as an app-level gate even when iOS still allows Always or While Using.
- Show when OpenClaw is Off but iOS still allows location, without treating the OS grant as consent to re-enable OpenClaw location.
- Stop background/significant-change monitoring when the user turns Location off or downgrades away from Always.
- Reconcile iOS Settings downgrades through CoreLocation delegate updates, including persisted significant-change monitor cleanup after process relaunch.

## Evidence

- Current head: `27bbbcd63a26f98e680ace56e1b924ce05e98779`.
- Current-head consent sync proof for preserving Off/While Using under broader iOS grants: https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/proof/pr-99247-location-always/proof/pr-99247/current-head-consent-sync-proof.md
- Final physical iPhone proof summary and contact sheet: https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/proof/pr-99247-location-always/proof/pr-99247/final-physical-video-summary.md
- Redacted terminal proof artifact with rank-up coverage mapping: https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/proof/pr-99247-location-always/proof/pr-99247/README.md
- iPhone life-test runbook for physical proof: https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/proof/pr-99247-location-always/proof/pr-99247/life-test-runbook.md
- Physical iPhone video observed: iOS Always grant, OpenClaw Always summary, OpenClaw While Using under broader iOS grant, iOS downgrade to While Using, OpenClaw Always + iOS While Using mismatch warning, spinner clearing, and usable picker through the mutations.
- After that video, head `27bbbcd63a26` fixes the remaining consent-model issues: external iOS Always/While Using grants no longer promote OpenClaw Location Off back to an enabled mode, and iOS Always no longer promotes explicit OpenClaw While Using to Always.
- `pnpm native:i18n:check` passed (`entries=2453 changed=false`).
- SwiftFormat lint passed for `LocationPermissionSummary.swift` and `LocationPermissionSummaryTests.swift`.
- SwiftLint strict passed for `LocationPermissionSummary.swift` and `LocationPermissionSummaryTests.swift`.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Focused simulator tests passed: `OpenClawTests/LocationPermissionSummaryTests` on iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5, 17 tests, covering Always/While Using mismatch, denied/global-disabled state, sticky Off under positive iOS grants, sticky While Using under iOS Always, downgrade cleanup, and significant-location monitoring eligibility.
- Built simulator app Info.plist includes `UIBackgroundModes = [audio, location, remote-notification]`.
- Prior proof build was installed on Polly's iPhone for physical recording using bundle `ai.openclawfoundation.app.test.pollybot-5y97h9j837`; local proof signing stripped personal-team entitlements, so the proof is scoped to the Location settings flow, not push/App Groups/share/widget/watch behavior.
- Local Codex review after the earlier ClawSweeper fix found no actionable regressions in the location permission summary, background monitoring controls, or Settings UI changes.

target.title: feat(qa): add transport capability and factory contracts
target.body:
Fixes #99622

## What Problem This Solves

QA Lab selected QA Channel and Crabline adapters through separate static and special-case paths. Canonical scenarios could not declare transport requirements, adapter capabilities were not versioned or machine-readable, and missing capabilities or unsupported operations did not share a closed error contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change adds one asynchronous `QaTransportAdapterFactory` registry for the existing QA Channel and Crabline adapters. Factories expose a versioned capability manifest, validate requested capabilities before adapter startup, verify declared operations against the created adapter, and normalize missing-capability, startup, credential-blocked, and unsupported-operation failures.

Scenario execution metadata now accepts `execution.transport.requiredCapabilities`. The existing channel streaming scenario declares text and preview-lifecycle requirements while retaining the established `waitForOutboundSequence` flow. Factory and suite cleanup covers capability rejection, adapter startup, provider startup, and Gateway startup failures.

The contract stays inside the QA Lab plugin boundary and consumes the existing `@openclaw/crabline@0.1.8` adapter/server API. Script evidence writing and scenario catalog ownership validation are unchanged.

## User Impact

No direct end-user behavior changes. QA maintainers and channel contributors get deterministic transport preflight, machine-readable capability declarations, consistent blocked/failure errors, and one adapter creation path for QA Channel and Crabline scenarios.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/qa-transport-contracts.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/qa-transport-registry.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-catalog.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-flow.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/suite.test.ts` — 5 files, 63 tests passed.
- Scoped `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` passed for all touched TypeScript files.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwmp6bm3xerp0nmys08xfwdm` — `check:changed` passed, including full typecheck, core/extensions/scripts lint, and runtime import-cycle validation.
- Codex autoreview — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Existing-solutions preflight found no maintained generic registry package that supplied the repository-specific transport lifecycle, capability manifest, and normalized error contract; the implementation reuses current QA Lab registry patterns and Crabline's published bridge API.

target.title: fix: cap Codex native tool output before replay
target.body:
Closes #99465
Related: #99551

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where oversized native Codex tool output could remain large enough in OpenClaw's Codex app-server projection surfaces to dominate replay-bound worker context even though visible transcript rendering had a separate truncation path.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one shared projector-side cap for native Codex tool output and routes snapshot command output, streamed command-output fallback text, dynamic/MCP projected output text, trajectory `tool.result` output, transcript tool-result messages, and emitted tool-result progress text through it. The cap is `10_000` characters including the truncation notice, and the notice includes the original character count plus the displayed cap.

The change does not claim to fix every future token runaway. It hardens the app-server projection boundary that was still allowing large output text to stay live after a small worker task produced repeated verbose tool results.

## User Impact

Operators and users should see oversized native tool output summarized with an explicit OpenClaw truncation notice instead of having very large command output copied into replay-bound Codex/OpenClaw projection surfaces. This reduces the chance that one verbose command result dominates later worker input tokens.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts`
  - 101 tests passed.
- `git diff --check`
  - Passed.

Additional local proof attempt:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts`
  - 115 tests passed.
  - 1 existing unrelated test timed out locally: `keeps managed web_search for provider-qualified Codex model overrides`.
- Targeted rerun of that single web-search override test stayed silent for about one minute and was interrupted for local resource safety.

Notes:

- No raw private worker transcript or session JSONL content is included in this PR.
- GitHub CI/Testbox should be treated as the broader integration proof for the `run-attempt` lane.
- AI-assisted change.

target.title: feat: add slash command picker in chat composer
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has many slash commands, but the chat composer did not provide an in-context way to discover, filter, and select them. Users had to know command names ahead of time, and invalid slash input could still reach send-time flows without clear composer-side handling.

This PR adds a slash command picker that opens when the user types `/`, supports category switching between commands and skills, filters results as the user types, and validates slash-style input before sending.

## Evidence

- Added focused Swift coverage for slash command picker state and send-time validation in `OpenClawKitTests/ChatViewModelTests.swift`.
- Added iOS gateway coverage in `apps/ios/Tests/IOSGatewayChatTransportTests.swift` for the command catalog transport surface.
- Captured UI screenshots from the implemented picker states:
  - Full picker: https://github.com/VicZhang6/openclaw/blob/assets/slash-screenshots/docs/assets/slash-panel-all.png?raw=true
  - Commands tab: https://github.com/VicZhang6/openclaw/blob/assets/slash-screenshots/docs/assets/slash-panel-commands.png?raw=true
  - Skills tab: https://github.com/VicZhang6/openclaw/blob/assets/slash-screenshots/docs/assets/slash-panel-skills.png?raw=true

## Design Philosophy

Since OpenClaw has many slash commands, the picker appears directly from the chat composer instead of requiring a separate reference page or memorized command names. The UI keeps the command name, description, and category visible so users can choose quickly without losing message context.

### Key Features

- **Instant trigger**: Type `/` to open the floating picker
- **Category tabs**: Switch between Commands and Skills views
- **Live filtering**: Start typing to filter the list in real time
- **Rich metadata**: Each item shows its name, description, and category badge
- **Send-time validation**: Invalid slash input is intercepted before sending

### Screenshots

**Full picker - all commands and skills**
![Slash Panel All](https://github.com/VicZhang6/openclaw/blob/assets/slash-screenshots/docs/assets/slash-panel-all.png?raw=true)

**Filtered to commands only**
![Slash Panel Commands](https://github.com/VicZhang6/openclaw/blob/assets/slash-screenshots/docs/assets/slash-panel-commands.png?raw=true)

target.title: Redact exec tool result payloads
target.body:
## Summary
- redact exec foreground tool-result text and structured `details.aggregated` before returning results to the agent
- redact node-host exec stdout/stderr/error output before formatting tool results
- redact process poll/log/list output and structured details that can include output tails or aggregated process output

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Exec and background process tool results could return secret-shaped stdout/stderr/session text back to the agent. This patch redacts those returned tool-result surfaces before they leave the exec/process/node-host formatters.

**Real environment tested:** Real local OpenClaw checkout on branch `fix/exec-tool-result-redaction` at `da701a0bbf6c`, using an isolated temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME`. The proof used an obvious fake canary value, not a real credential.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran a local runtime proof that exercised `createExecTool` and `createProcessTool` with a fake `REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET` value, then inspected the returned tool-result `content[0].text` and structured `details.aggregated` values for foreground exec, process poll, process log, and process list tail/details surfaces.

**Evidence after fix:** Copied live output from the local runtime proof:

```json
{
  "foregroundExec": {
    "status": "completed",
    "text": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890",
    "detailsAggregated": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890",
    "rawCanaryValuePresent": false,
    "redactedMarkerPresent": true
  },
  "processPoll": {
    "status": "completed",
    "text": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890\n\n\nProcess exited with code 0.",
    "detailsAggregated": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890\n",
    "rawCanaryValuePresent": false,
    "redactedMarkerPresent": true
  },
  "processLog": {
    "status": "completed",
    "text": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890",
    "detailsAggregated": "",
    "rawCanaryValuePresent": false,
    "redactedMarkerPresent": true
  },
  "processList": {
    "status": "completed",
    "textTail": "REDACTION_CANARY_SECRET=clawsw…7890",
    "rawCanaryValuePresent": false,
    "redactedMarkerPresent": true
  }
}
```

Supplemental focused regression coverage also exercises node-host exec stdout redaction by passing a fake node `system.run` payload through `executeNodeHostCommand` and asserting both returned text and `details.aggregated` redact the raw canary.

**Observed result after fix:** The raw fake canary value was absent from returned foreground exec, process poll, process log, and process list output. Redacted markers were present in the returned text/details where output was expected. The node-host formatter path is covered by the focused regression test for the same returned tool-result boundary.

**What was not tested:** Live node-host exec against a physical connected node was unavailable in this isolated proof environment; the node-host formatter was validated with the focused regression test that feeds a fake gateway node response through the production formatter path.

target.title: fix(watch-node): defer restart when dist/entry.js is missing mid-rebuild
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: When a git pull triggers source file changes while `dist/` is mid-rebuild, the hot-reload watcher (`watch-node.mjs`) kills the current healthy gateway process and restarts into a missing `dist/entry.js`, causing an 8x crash-loop that exhausts systemd's restart limit.

**Solution**: Check build readiness before restarting. The new `isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs)` function verifies that both `dist/entry.js` exists AND the build stamp's git HEAD matches the current checkout HEAD. If either check fails (missing entry, mismatched HEAD, missing stamp, or stamp without HEAD), the restart is deferred and polled every 2s until the build is verified fresh. An additional guard in the child-process exit handler prevents crash-looping when the watcher would otherwise restart into a stale build after a child exit.

**What changed**: Two files — `scripts/watch-node.mjs` and `test/scripts/watch-node.test.ts`.

**What did NOT change**: Build logic (`tsdown-build.mjs`), source watch paths, the `dist/` IGNORE segment, or `run-node.mjs`.

Fixes #99603

## What Problem This Solves

Production gateway deployments using a git checkout with hot-reload (via systemd) are vulnerable to a crash-loop when a `git pull` triggers a rebuild while `dist/` is mid-build. The watcher kills the currently-healthy gateway and restarts into a missing entrypoint. This caused a 37-minute production outage on 2026-07-03.

## Root Cause

`watch-node.mjs:requestRestart()` unconditionally sends SIGTERM to the healthy gateway child process whenever chokidar detects a relevant source file change (e.g. from `git pull`). During a rebuild, `tsdown-build.mjs` calls `cleanTsdownOutputRoots()` which removes `dist/entry.js`. The new child then crashes because the entrypoint doesn't exist, and `shouldRestartAfterChildExit()` treats SIGTERM/exit code 143 as restartable — forming a crash-loop.

**Additionally**: Even when an old `dist/entry.js` exists, the current git HEAD may have changed (after `git pull`), meaning `run-node` will rebuild and clean `dist` after the stop. The old entrypoint check alone is insufficient to prevent the crash-loop.

## Changes

`scripts/watch-node.mjs` (+86 / -37 lines):

### Layer 1 — `isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs, resolveHead)`

Replaces the previous `isDistEntryFresh()` mtime check with a comprehensive build-readiness check:
- Verifies `dist/entry.js` exists (basic guard for mid-rebuild window)
- Reads the `.buildstamp` file from `dist/` and compares its recorded `head` against the current checkout HEAD via `resolveGitHead()`
- If HEADs differ, or if the stamp lacks a `head` but the current HEAD is known, the build is stale — restart is deferred
- Falls back gracefully (entry-only check) when git or stamp file is unavailable

### Layer 2 — Deferred polling (existing, retained)

When build is not ready, polls every 2s instead of dropping the restart request. When the build completes (entry.js + matching stamp appear), auto-triggers the restart.

### Layer 3 — Exit handler guard

On child-process exit (SIGTERM/143), verifies build readiness before restarting. Prevents self-reinforcing crash-loop when the child exits during a rebuild window.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: The hot-reload watcher no longer kills the current healthy gateway child process when the build output is missing or stale for the current checkout.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v22 — L2 evidence via direct function call with real `fs` module and real `resolveGitHead()` against the worktree git checkout.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```terminal
node evidence-collection.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence**:

```terminal
======================================================================
L2 Evidence: isBuildReadyForRestart with real fs/git
======================================================================

1. Current git HEAD: 0aeb43d2cc69...

--- Scenario A: Missing dist/entry.js ---
   isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs) = false (expected: false)

--- Scenario B: entry.js + matching build stamp ---
   Created: dist/.buildstamp with head: 0aeb43d2cc69...
   isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs) = true (expected: true)

--- Scenario C: entry.js + MISMATCHED build stamp ---
   Updated: dist/.buildstamp with head: 00000000... (mismatched)
   isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs) = false (expected: false)

--- Scenario D: entry.js exists, NO build stamp ---
   Removed: dist/.buildstamp
   isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs) = false (expected: false)
======================================================================
```

**Observed result after the fix**: `isBuildReadyForRestart` returns `true` only when entry.js exists AND the build stamp HEAD matches the current checkout HEAD. Scenario C directly demonstrates the fix for the review finding: even when an old `dist/entry.js` exists (simulating a `git pull` that changed the checkout), a mismatched git HEAD causes the restart to be deferred, preventing the crash-loop. 17/17 unit tests pass covering all code paths.

**What was not tested**: Real Gateway integration with live systemd restart race (requires controlled git-pull-triggered rebuild environment). The pure-function and exit-handler tests provide L2 coverage for all code paths.

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Low risk — change is constrained to `isBuildReadyForRestart()` guard logic in `requestRestart()` and the exit handler; no impact on build, runtime, or non-watch paths
- [x] All behaviors are additive (check before kill); when build stamp matches, behavior is identical to current code
- [x] 17 tests added/updated covering all code paths including stamp matching, stamp-without-head edge case, deferred restart, exit handler guard, and shutdown races
- [x] No config, API, or dependency changes
- [x] Does not affect production (non-watch) gateway usage

## Review

- Manually reviewed and verified
- AI-assisted: Yes

target.title: fix: Mattermost interaction token forgeable via hardcoded HMAC...
target.body:
## Fix Summary
The `deriveInteractionSecret` function in the Mattermost extension uses a hardcoded public string as the HMAC key, making the interaction signing secret fully reproducible by anyone who knows the bot token. An attacker who obtains the bot token can forge valid `_token` values, craft arbitrary button-click POST requests to the gateway's interaction endpoint, and trigger agent system events (`core.system.enqueueSystemEvent`) as if a legitimate user clicked an approved Mattermost button.

## Issue Linkage
Fixes #64545

## Security Snapshot
- CVSS v3.1: 7.1 (High)
- CVSS v4.0: 7.1 (High)

## Implementation Details
### Files Changed

target.title: fix: recover stranded replies in message_tool_only mode (#85714)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.visibleReplies` is set to `message_tool`, the agent is expected to call the message tool to deliver replies. If the LLM forgets (a probabilistic event — the reporter saw it happen on the 8th turn after 7 correct deliveries), the reply was **silently discarded**: the substantive text sat in the JSONL transcript but was never delivered to the user.

The existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal()` detection was already identifying these stranded replies and logging a warning, but took no recovery action.

## Fix

This commit promotes the detection from log-only to **followup retry**, preserving the `message_tool_only` privacy contract:

1. **Gate room events**: Skip stranded reply detection for ambient `room_event` turns where `message_tool_only` is automatically set by the system. Silence on room events is intentional by design — the agent chose not to respond.

2. **Enqueue followup retry turn**: When a stranded reply is detected, enqueue a followup run whose prompt instructs the agent to deliver the captured text via `message(action=send)`. The agent itself calls the message tool, so delivery happens through the correct contract path — no suppression bypass, no privacy boundary crossing.

3. **Clear transcript/persistence fields**: The retry run explicitly clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` from the original followup run to prevent the original user prompt from hiding the retry instruction. The followup runner resolves `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text`, so a retained `transcriptPrompt` would cause the agent to see the original user question instead of the retry delivery instruction.

4. **No suppression bypass**: This does NOT mark payloads with `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or use `skipSuppressionCheck`. The `message_tool_only` privacy contract is fully preserved: delivery only happens when the agent explicitly calls `message(action=send)`.

Normal (non-stranded) paths are unaffected: short replies, intentional `NO_REPLY`, and runs where the message tool already delivered are all excluded by the existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal` guard.

### Why followup retry instead of bypass delivery?

The `message_tool_only` contract says: "no message tool call = private/silent". Auto-publishing stranded text would break this documented behavior. Instead, we give the agent a second chance to follow the contract correctly — like returning an undelivered letter and asking the sender to mail it properly, rather than opening and publishing it ourselves.

## Changed files

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — followup retry with cleaned transcript fields, room_event gate (+26/-3 net)
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — 5 new retry/gate tests replacing 6 bypass tests (-4 net)

## Tests

| Suite | Count | Status |
|-------|-------|--------|
| `agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` | 47 | ✅ All pass |
| `private-message-tool-final.test.ts` | 8 | ✅ All pass |
| `dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | 189 | ✅ All pass (unchanged, confirms no regressions) |
| `followup-runner.test.ts` | 67 | ✅ All pass (confirms followup queue compatibility) |

New test cases:
- `enqueues a followup retry for a stranded substantive reply (#85714)` — verifies `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with retry prompt containing the assistant text
- `does not enqueue retry for short private final replies` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry when the message tool delivered this turn` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry for room_event turns (#85714)` — verifies room_event gate
- `clears transcriptPrompt on retry to prevent original prompt from hiding retry instruction (#85714)` — regression test verifying `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` are all `undefined` on the retry run

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent's final message silently discarded when LLM forgets to call the message tool in `message_tool_only` mode. The fix enqueues a followup retry turn so the agent can deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract.
- **Real environment tested**: Local macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, patched checkout at `9dc3c76dc3`.
- **Privacy contract preserved**: The fix does NOT use `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or `skipSuppressionCheck`. No payload is auto-delivered. The agent is re-prompted to call `message(action=send)` itself.
- **Transcript isolation**: The retry run clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` so the followup runner's `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text` resolution correctly uses the retry prompt, not the original user message.
- **Room event safety**: Stranded reply detection is gated by `sessionCtx.InboundEventKind !== "room_event"`, so ambient room events (where silence is intentional) never trigger recovery. Covered by dedicated test case.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, `warnPrivateMessageToolFinal` only logs — no retry is enqueued and the reply is silently lost.
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  ✓ auto-reply agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts (47 tests) 1729ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  47 passed (47)

  ✓ unit-fast private-message-tool-final.test.ts (8 tests) 2ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  8 passed (8)

  ✓ auto-reply dispatch-from-config.test.ts (189 tests) 3770ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  189 passed (189)

  ✓ auto-reply followup-runner.test.ts (67 tests) 1710ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  67 passed (67)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: When a stranded reply is detected, `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with a retry prompt containing the original assistant text and instructions to call `message(action=send)`. The retry run has `transcriptPrompt: undefined` so the followup runner correctly uses the retry instruction. Short replies, already-delivered replies, room events, and runs with existing transcript prompts are all verified by dedicated test cases.
- **What was not tested**: Live end-to-end delivery through an actual channel — the test verifies that the correct followup run is enqueued with the expected prompt shape and cleaned fields. The followup queue machinery (`enqueueFollowupRun` → `scheduleFollowupDrain` → `runReplyAgent`) is a well-tested existing mechanism used for concurrent message queuing.

## Real behavior proof (end-to-end, qa-lab host runner)

This adds a deterministic end-to-end proof that drives the real runtime loop — `runReplyAgent → stranded-final detection → warnPrivateMessageToolFinal → enqueueFollowupRun("stranded-reply-retry") → followup-runner → runEmbeddedAgent → message(action=send) → qa-channel outbound` — not the unit mocks (which stub `enqueueFollowupRun`/`runEmbeddedAgent`).

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Under `messages.visibleReplies=message_tool` (resolved `message_tool_only`), a substantive final reply that never calls the message tool was kept private and silently lost. The fix detects the stranded final and enqueues exactly one bounded followup retry that re-prompts the agent to deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract; if the retry strands again, no second retry is enqueued.
- **Real environment tested**: macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, branch `fix/stranded-reply-pending-delivery-85714` at current HEAD `0469009210` (rebased on latest upstream/main; recovery default-off + collect-batching isolation + updated scenario). qa-lab host runner: in-process gateway child + qa-channel bus + scenario-aware `mock-openai` provider (deterministic by construction; no live model, no Docker).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: ran the new scenario, PASS:
  ```
  node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite \
    --provider-mode mock-openai \
    --scenario message-tool-stranded-final-recovery \
    --concurrency 1 --fast
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: captured scenario result and the gateway's own runtime log line (ids redacted):
  ```
  COUNTS: { total: 1, passed: 1, failed: 0 }
  step: pass - recovered=1; stranded turns=1; retry delivery turns=1; WARN logged=true

  2026-06-06T06:31:23.411+08:00 [source-reply/private-final] agent produced a long private final reply without calling the configured delivery tool (message_tool_only); response kept private and not delivered to the source channel
  ```
  Asserted from the live request/outbound capture:
  - Turn 1 request: `plannedToolName !== "message"` (long plain-text final, stranded).
  - Exactly one retry request plans the message tool, detected via the verbatim retry needle `you did not call message(action=send)`.
  - Retry delivery request: `plannedToolName === "message"`, `plannedToolArgs.action === "send"`, `plannedToolArgs.message === "QA-STRANDED-85714"`; one outbound on the direct conversation carried the marker (`recovered=1`).
  - After an 8s settle: outbound with the marker stays exactly 1 and message-tool retry deliveries stay exactly 1 (no loop).
- **Observed result after fix**: the stranded `message_tool_only` final was detected and warned, exactly one retry was enqueued, the retry delivered the original text via `message(action=send)` to the channel, and no second retry/delivery occurred — all four invariants observed against the real delivery path.
- **What was not tested**: not run against a live frontier model (deterministic mock by design, since a real model "forgetting" the tool is non-deterministic), and not on a real chat transport (Telegram/WhatsApp/Discord) — exercised on the in-process qa-channel bus; the `message(action=send)` → source-conversation outbound contract is transport-agnostic core auto-reply behavior.

Proof scaffolding added (business logic under `src/auto-reply/` untouched): `qa/scenarios/channels/message-tool-stranded-final-recovery.md` (new scenario) and `extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.ts` (two additive deterministic decision branches following the existing `qa group visible reply tool check` pattern).

Closes #85714







## Update — retry drain scheduling (follow-up)

Refined the stranded-reply retry enqueue so it no longer restarts the followup drain while the active reply operation still owns the lane. The retry now enqueues with `restartIfIdle=false` and routes the drain through `scheduleFollowupDrainAfterReplyOperationClear` (the same owner-clear path the normal followup enqueue uses), so the retry only runs once the owning operation releases the lane — removing a potential race with the owner-clear handoff.

- **Changed**: `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — stranded retry enqueue mirrors the normal enqueue-followup path (dormant enqueue + deferred drain).
- **Test**: `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — added `schedules the stranded-reply retry drain only after the active reply operation clears`, asserting the drain stays dormant while the reply operation owns the lane and fires only after it clears.
- **Verification after this change** (local, macOS arm64, Node v24.10.0):
  ```
  vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts  ->  55 passed (55)
  tsgo:core (prod typecheck)        ->  pass
  tsgo:test:src (test typecheck)    ->  pass
  oxlint (touched files)            ->  pass
  ```

target.title: feat: expose model pricing to plugins via runtime.usage API
target.body:
## Summary
Adds a `runtime.usage` namespace to the plugin runtime, exposing `resolveModelCostConfig()` and `estimateUsageCost()` so context engine plugins can calculate model-cost estimates from OpenClaw's configured pricing instead of hardcoded heuristics.

## Motivation
Context engine plugins, such as [ContextClaw](https://github.com/dodge1218/contextclaw), truncate stale or large context to save tokens. Today they can only estimate savings with a fixed heuristic. OpenClaw already has per-model pricing through `resolveModelCostConfig`; this PR threads those helpers through the plugin runtime so plugins can use the same pricing source as the host.

## Changes
- `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-usage.ts` — adds the runtime usage facade.
- `src/plugins/runtime/types-core.ts` — adds the `usage` namespace to `PluginRuntimeCore`.
- `src/plugins/runtime/index.ts` — wires `createRuntimeUsage()` into runtime assembly.
- `src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/plugin-runtime-mock.ts` — updates the plugin runtime mock.
- `src/plugins/runtime/index.test.ts` — asserts the runtime exposes both usage helpers.
- `docs/plugins/sdk-runtime.md` — documents the plugin SDK usage helpers.
- `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` — regenerates the public SDK API baseline.

## Real Behavior Proof
- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A plugin can access the new `api.runtime.usage` namespace and call both pricing helpers without importing OpenClaw internals.

- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout on branch `feat/plugin-cost-api` at `39b243468f`, after rebasing onto upstream `main` and narrowing the PR to the plugin runtime/docs/test surface.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
pnpm exec tsx .artifacts/pr64436-runtime-usage-proof/run-direct-plugin-api-proof.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal output from a minimal external plugin fixture with `openclaw.plugin.json` plus `index.mjs`; its `register(api)` calls `api.runtime.usage.resolveModelCostConfig(...)` and `api.runtime.usage.estimateUsageCost(...)`.

```text

[proof] pluginDir=/tmp/openclaw-runtime-usage-direct-ile3Im
[proof] manifest=/tmp/openclaw-runtime-usage-direct-ile3Im/openclaw.plugin.json

[plugin] estimateUsageCost total=0.010950
[proof] PASS plugin register(api) called both api.runtime.usage helpers
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The plugin saw `api.runtime.usage`, resolved the configured proof model cost, estimated usage cost as `0.010950`, and exited with the PASS line above.

- **What was not tested:** Full OpenClaw app startup and provider billing reconciliation; this proof is scoped to the plugin runtime API surface added by this PR.

## Local Verification

target.body:
## Summary

Adds support for Anthropic's **advisor tool** (beta: `advisor-tool-2026-03-01`), a server-side tool that lets Claude consult a separate model instance during inference. Also adds generic handling for all server-side tool blocks (`server_tool_use`, `*_tool_result`) which were previously silently dropped by the transport stream.

Fixes several latent issues discovered along the way:
- `mapStopReason` no longer crashes on unknown stop reasons (now maps `compaction`/`model_context_window_exceeded` to `length`)
- All display text derived from API responses is now sanitized via `sanitizeTransportPayloadText`
- Advisor model config accepts provider-qualified refs (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`)

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Auth / tokens

- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #63930 (Feature request + design rationale + session log)
- [x] This PR adds a new feature

## Root Cause / Motivation

OpenClaw's Anthropic transport silently drops all server-side tool content blocks. This means:
- Users can't enable the new advisor beta tool
- `web_search` and `code_execution` tool invocations don't appear in transcripts
- `mapStopReason` throws on novel stop reasons, crashing the transport

This PR adds the missing handling.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

### New: advisor tool support
Enable in `openclaw.json`:
```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "models": {
        "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6": {
          "params": { "advisor": true }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```
Or with a custom advisor model:
```json
{
  "params": {
    "advisor": { "enabled": true, "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6" }
  }
}
```

When the model consults the advisor, its output appears inline as `[Advisor] ...` text in the conversation.

### Changed: server-side tool block handling
- `server_tool_use` (advisor, web_search, code_execution) — silently dropped (these are invocation markers, not content)
- `*_tool_result` with readable text → text block with `serverToolDisplay: true` flag (visible in UI, skipped on API replay to keep transcript clean)
- `*_tool_result` without readable text → silently dropped
- `mapStopReason` now maps `model_context_window_exceeded` and `compaction` to `"length"` (previously would throw)

## Diagram

```text
Before:
  content_block_start { type: "server_tool_use" } → silently dropped
  content_block_start { type: "advisor_tool_result" } → silently dropped
  stop_reason: "compaction" → throws Error

After:
  server_tool_use → dropped (invocation marker)
  advisor_tool_result(advisor_result, text) → text block "[Advisor] ..." with serverToolDisplay:true
  advisor_tool_result(advisor_redacted_result) → text block "[Advisor output (encrypted)]"
  advisor_tool_result(advisor_tool_result_error) → text block "[Advisor error: <code>]"
  compaction → maps to "length"

convertAnthropicMessages:
  text blocks with serverToolDisplay: true → skipped on replay
  (keeps API transcript clean without polluting multi-turn context)
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? **No**
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? **No**
- New/changed network calls? **Yes** — adds `advisor-tool-2026-03-01` beta header when advisor is enabled. Only applies to Anthropic API requests for Claude models.
- Command/tool execution surface changed? **No** — advisor is server-side, runs inside Anthropic's infrastructure, no local execution
- Data access scope changed? **No**

### Security hardening included

- All display text derived from API responses is sanitized via `sanitizeTransportPayloadText` (prevents terminal escape sequence injection from compromised responses)
- Advisor model config uses strict regex validation (`/^claude-[a-z0-9.-]+$/`) — rejects non-Claude models with a warning instead of sending invalid requests
- `!Array.isArray()` guard on advisor config object
- Tool name collision detection — warns if a user-defined `advisor` tool exists instead of creating a duplicate
- `mapStopReason` hardening prevents throws on unknown API stop reasons

## Repro + Verification

### Environment
- OS: macOS (Darwin 24.6.0)
- Runtime: Node 24.8, pnpm 10.32
- Model/provider: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` via Anthropic API
- Config: `params.advisor: true` in `openclaw.json`

### Steps
1. Configure OpenClaw with Anthropic provider and advisor enabled
2. Run the agent pipeline: `openclaw agent --local --agent main -m "<complex question>"`
3. Observe `[Advisor] ...` text in the response for questions that trigger advisor consultation
4. Verify via debug logs: `advisor tool injected: model=claude-sonnet-4-6 totalTools=N`

### Expected
- Advisor tool is injected into every Anthropic request when `params.advisor: true`
- Advisor-tool-2026-03-01 beta header is present on requests
- When the model invokes the advisor, its output appears inline in the response
- Server-side tool block handling does not crash the transport
- `mapStopReason` handles all known stop reasons without throwing

### Actual
Matches expected. Live API validation scripts (`scripts/validate-*.ts`) confirm both `web_search` and `advisor` tool flows produce the expected SSE events.

## Evidence

- [x] **329 tests pass** — full `pnpm test` suite
- [x] **51/51 extension tests pass** — `pnpm test:extension anthropic`
- [x] **17 new transport tests** — advisor flow, mapStopReason resilience, server-side tool translation, redacted result handling
- [x] **6 new stream-wrapper tests** — config resolution, wrapper composition, name collision detection, non-Claude rejection
- [x] **1 new chat-content test** — `serverToolDisplay` extraction
- [x] **Live API validation** — two scripts confirm real Anthropic responses work correctly
- [x] **End-to-end agent pipeline verified** — `advisor tool injected: totalTools=27` confirmed via debug log

## Human Verification (required)

### Verified scenarios
- Live API call with `web_search` tool — observed `server_tool_use(name=web_search)` + `web_search_tool_result` + `code_execution_tool_result` with `encrypted_content` fields
- Live API call with `advisor` tool — observed `server_tool_use(name=advisor)` + `advisor_tool_result(advisor_result, text)` + text response
- Agent pipeline end-to-end — advisor tool visible in outgoing request payload (tool #27 of 27), model responds successfully
- Config validation — `advisor: { model: "gpt-4" }` correctly rejected with warning
- Config validation — `advisor: { model: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6" }` accepted (provider prefix stripped)
- Duplicate tool detection — warns when a custom tool named `advisor` already exists

### Edge cases checked
- Unknown `stop_reason` values (e.g. `some_future_reason`) → maps to `"stop"` without throwing
- `compaction` and `model_context_window_exceeded` stop reasons → map to `"length"`
- `advisor_redacted_result` content → displays as `[Advisor output (encrypted)]`
- `advisor_tool_result_error` content → displays as `[Advisor error: <code>]`
- Untranslatable `web_search_tool_result` (array content) → silently dropped (no prompt pollution)
- Malformed advisor config (array, null, wrong type) → handled gracefully

### What I did not verify
- Multi-turn conversations where an encrypted advisor result must be replayed verbatim (documented as a known limitation — the API continues fine without it)
- Non-Anthropic provider fallback after an advisor turn (documented tradeoff — the `[Advisor]` text survives as normal conversation context, which preserves information for the fallback model)
- Advisor sub-inference cost/usage surfacing (deferred to follow-up)

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? **Yes** — existing conversations without advisor config are unchanged
- Config/env changes? **No** — the `params` field is an open `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`, no schema change needed
- Migration needed? **No**

## Risks and Mitigations

### Known limitations (follow-up work)

1. **Encrypted content round-tripping**: `advisor_redacted_result.encrypted_content` and `web_search_tool_result` encrypted blobs are not sent back to the API on subsequent turns. The SDK says these "must be round-tripped verbatim," but live testing confirms the API continues fine without them — the model just loses encrypted context from prior server-side tool calls. Full round-tripping would require integration with the existing pruning/context-sizing pipeline (to avoid unbounded context growth from retained encrypted payloads). Deferred to a follow-up PR.

2. **Cost tracking**: Advisor sub-inference tokens (`usage.iterations` array) are not yet surfaced in `TransportUsage`. Adding them requires careful integration with the existing cost pipeline to avoid inflating `totalTokens` (which drives flush/compaction decisions). Deferred.

3. **Cross-provider fallback**: If a session switches from Anthropic to OpenAI/Google mid-conversation, `[Advisor] ...` text survives as normal assistant text in the replayed history. This is intentional — stripping it would lose conversation context for the fallback model. Documented in code comments.

### Risk: Anthropic changes advisor tool schema
- **Mitigation**: The beta header (`advisor-tool-2026-03-01`) is version-pinned. Future versions can be added alongside without breaking existing behavior.

### Risk: A user defines a custom tool named `advisor` that conflicts with our injection
- **Mitigation**: `createAnthropicAdvisorToolWrapper` checks for existing `advisor` tools before injection and warns on conflict instead of creating duplicates.

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` gained an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline and `sanitizeUserFacingText`, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer), no new public SDK surface is added, and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Local validation:

```
node scripts/test-projects.mjs (affected test files): pass (sanitizer + promotion + agents)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. new whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test: clean
oxlint on changed source files: 0 warnings, 0 errors
oxfmt --check on changed files: all correctly formatted
```

target.title: fix: accept valid MCP tool schemas without strict inputSchema.type check
target.body:
## Summary
Fixes MCP server loading failure when tools have `inputSchema` without explicit `type: "object"`.

Closes #63602

## Changes
- `listAllTools` validates each `tools/list` page **once** with `RelaxedListToolsResultSchema` and catalogs **that same validated payload** — there is no strict-then-relist flow, so a stateful or hostile server cannot pass validation with one response and have a different response consumed (no validation-to-use gap).
- `RelaxedToolSchema` is **derived from the pinned SDK's own `ToolSchema`** (`ToolSchema.extend` / `ToolSchema.shape.inputSchema.extend`) and differs from it at exactly one point: the root `inputSchema.type` is an optional string instead of `z.literal("object")`. Every other field — `outputSchema`, task `execution` metadata, `annotations`, pagination — keeps the exact pinned SDK contract, so malformed metadata still rejects the page.
- After every page parse, the SDK's `cacheToolMetadata()` is invoked with the validated tools — the same side effect `client.listTools()` runs — so `callTool()` enforces output-schema validation and task-required guards identically to the SDK flow. The call is optional (no crash if a future SDK removes the method) and a dedicated test pins the method's existence so a dependency upgrade that drops it fails loudly rather than silently shedding the guards.
- `normalizeInputSchema()` backfills `type: "object"` only when the field is missing; `isValidRootInputSchema()` + the catalog gate skip tools with an explicit non-object root type (e.g. `"string"`, `"array"`) with a `logWarn`. Server `toolCount` reports accepted tools only.

## Root Cause
The MCP SDK v1.29.0 `ToolSchema` validates `inputSchema.type` as `z.literal("object")`. Some MCP servers (especially older SDKs or custom implementations) omit `type` from `inputSchema`, returning `{ properties: { ... } }`, which trips a Zod validation error: `invalid_value expected "object" in inputSchema.type` and crashes the whole catalog.

## v6 notes (current revision)
Addresses the P1 from the latest review (validation-to-use gap, confidence 0.96) by adopting its recommended repair: single-response validation that differs from the pinned SDK `ToolSchema` only at the root `inputSchema.type`, with SDK-equivalent metadata caching, explicit non-object filtering, and pagination preserved.
- The strict-then-relist flow is gone entirely; the request count per page is 1 in all cases.
- New stateful-server regression: a server that returns a benign typeless payload on request 1 and a malicious payload on request 2 gets exactly one `tools/list` request, and only the validated payload is cataloged. **Mutation-checked**: against the previous strict-then-relist implementation this test fails with the catalog containing the drifted (never-strictly-validated) tool — reproducing the reported attack — and the server log showing two list requests.
- New SDK-seam pin test: `Client.prototype.cacheToolMetadata` must exist, making the documented private-method dependency an explicit, loudly-failing audit point on SDK upgrades (P1 risk #2 from the same review).
- Relaxation-scope unit tests: malformed `outputSchema`, malformed `execution.taskSupport`, and missing `inputSchema` all still reject the page; pagination (`nextCursor`) keeps the SDK contract.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior or issue addressed: Bundle MCP tool cataloging accepts tools whose root `inputSchema` omits `type` by validating each `tools/list` response once against a schema derived from the pinned SDK contract (relaxed only at the root `inputSchema.type`), backfills `type: "object"`, skips explicit non-object roots, keeps servers with unrelated strict failures rejected, never issues a second list request, and preserves the SDK's `cacheToolMetadata()` side effects for every page.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS from the rebased PR head, Node 25.2.1, pnpm 11.2.2, driving the real bundle MCP runtime (`getOrCreateSessionMcpRuntime` → `getCatalog()` → `callTool()`) against four real out-of-process stdio MCP servers, one of them stateful (different payload per request).

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Ran `pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`, and `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1` on both files, plus a live four-server e2e script via `pnpm exec tsx`.

Evidence after fix:
```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  42 passed (42)
pnpm tsgo:core / tsgo:core:test: clean
oxlint / oxfmt --check: clean

e2e (four live stdio servers):
tools: ["legacySdkServer/search_docs","driftServer/benign_typeless_tool"]
servers: {"legacySdkServer":{"toolCount":1},"driftServer":{"toolCount":1}}
rejected: ["badOutputServer","mixedServer"]
driftServer tools/list requests received: 1        // exactly one — no second-request window
callTool(search_docs) → McpError -32600: Tool search_docs has an output schema but did not
  return structured content                        // metadata cache populated from the same response
```

Observed result after fix: A `tools/list` payload whose `inputSchema` omits `type` catalogs cleanly with `type: "object"` backfilled; an explicit `type: "array"` sibling is skipped with a logWarn; servers with malformed `outputSchema` (alone or mixed with a repairable tool) stay rejected; a stateful server attempting response drift receives exactly one list request and only its validated payload is cataloged; `callTool()` enforces `outputSchema` for typeless tools exactly as the SDK strict flow would.

What was not tested: A live third-party MCP server connected to an actual model-provider tool call was not tested in this environment.

## What Problem This Solves

The shared script evidence writer introduced by #99374 bounds logs and failure details, but it does not redact secret-bearing diagnostics or producer-known private values before persisting them. A truncation boundary can also retain a suffix of sensitive message content unless redaction happens before bounded output discards bytes.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follow-up reuses the existing logging redactor and adds producer-supplied sensitive values to `createQaScriptEvidenceWriter`. The writer removes exact sensitive values before generic masking, retains enough stream overlap to redact values split across child-process chunks, and only then applies the existing byte limits.

The focused contract tests cover credentials, access tokens, Matrix session keys, recovery material, private message content, chunk and byte-boundary splits, and native artifact content that claims a conflicting status.

## User Impact

There is no product behavior change. QA maintainers get bounded script evidence that does not persist known secret or private diagnostic content, while normalized pass/fail/blocked status remains controlled by the script result rather than native artifact payloads.

target.title: fix(gateway): use already-aborted signal in stopChannel fallback
target.body:
## Summary

- In `stopChannel`, when no `AbortController` exists for an account (i.e. no running task), the fallback `new AbortController().signal` creates a signal from an anonymous controller that **can never be aborted**
- `stopAccount` implementations may use this signal for cleanup coordination (checking `signal.aborted`, passing to `fetch`, using with `sleepWithAbort`, etc.)
- A never-aborting signal can cause `stopAccount` to hang or timeout during graceful shutdown instead of completing immediately

### Fix

Replace `new AbortController().signal` with `AbortSignal.abort()`, which returns an already-aborted signal. This correctly communicates "this account is being stopped" to the plugin's `stopAccount` implementation.

### Context

On line 485, `abort?.abort()` is called — so if `abort` exists, its signal is already aborted. The fallback only fires when `abort` is undefined (no active task for this account). In both cases the intent is the same: tell `stopAccount` to shut down. `AbortSignal.abort()` makes the fallback consistent with the primary path.

## Test plan

- [x] All 14 tests in `server-channels.test.ts` pass
- [x] One-line change, minimal risk
- [x] `AbortSignal.abort()` is available since Node 15.12.0; project requires Node 22+

target.title: feat: clarify iOS Location Always permission flow
target.body:
Related: #99229
Related: #86217
Related closed candidate: #99235

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where iOS users could select Location Always in OpenClaw without the app clearly explaining whether iOS had actually granted background-capable location access. That made wake-up/location workflows ambiguous when iOS only allowed While Using, denied access, global Location Services were disabled, or the user changed OpenClaw/iOS location settings independently.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an explicit iOS permission summary for Location settings that separates the user's selected OpenClaw mode from the effective iOS authorization state. It also wires the background-location contract into the native configuration and location service path: background updates are only enabled for Always-capable use, significant-change monitoring is stopped when the mode is disabled, downgraded, or no longer authorized Always, and app-level Location Off remains a sticky OpenClaw preference even when iOS still grants permission.

This follows the current SettingsProTab pattern for now because #99231 may reshape the Settings UI.

#99235 explored a similar area but was closed after it expanded beyond the Location Always flow. This PR keeps the scope narrower: Location permission copy, native i18n inventory, Info.plist background location declaration, background/significant-change monitoring gates, and focused tests.

## User Impact

Users get clearer feedback when Location Always is selected but iOS has not granted background-capable permission. Operators and reviewers also get a cleaner contract for when the iOS app may use background location behavior.

Use cases covered:

- Keep OpenClaw reachable for location-triggered/background wake-up workflows when the user explicitly selects Always and iOS grants Always.
- Show a warning when Always is selected but iOS only grants While Using, so users understand background location will not work.
- Preserve the selected Always mode in that mismatch state instead of reverting to the previous app setting.
- Show a warning when location is denied, restricted, or globally disabled in iOS settings.
- Preserve OpenClaw Location Off as an app-level gate even when iOS still allows Always or While Using.
- Show when OpenClaw is Off but iOS still allows location, without treating the OS grant as consent to re-enable OpenClaw location.
- Stop background/significant-change monitoring when the user turns Location off or downgrades away from Always.
- Reconcile iOS Settings downgrades through CoreLocation delegate updates, including persisted significant-change monitor cleanup after process relaunch.

target.title: fix(usage): handle Daylight saving time (DST) hour boundaries
target.body:
## Summary

This fixes a Control UI Usage-page freeze when a long session spans a local Daylight saving time (DST) transition.

Today the hour-slicing code computes a local `:59:59.999` hour end from the current wall-clock time. In a repeated local hour at Daylight saving time (DST) fallback, that can resolve to an earlier instant and stop cursor progress.

This change switches Usage hour slicing and selected-hour filtering to monotonic next-hour-boundary stepping so aggregation always moves forward in the selected timezone.

## Why

This fixes cases where:

- Usage is rendered in local time
- a session spans a Daylight saving time (DST) fallback or spring-forward boundary
- the page builds hour buckets or applies a selected-hour filter

Without this change, the Control UI can wedge the browser main thread while rendering Usage data for long sessions.

## Changes

- replace the ambiguous local end-of-hour calculation with `getNextHourStart()` plus bounded next-hour stepping in `ui/src/ui/views/usage-metrics.ts`
- convert session hour slicing to half-open intervals `[cursor, nextBoundary)` so exact boundaries do not create zero-duration buckets
- route the selected-hour filter in `ui/src/ui/views/usage.ts` through the same DST-safe helper instead of maintaining a duplicate loop
- add focused node-side regression coverage for Daylight saving time (DST) fallback, Daylight saving time (DST) spring-forward, peak-error aggregation, and full Usage render with an hour filter

## Testing

AI-assisted: yes
Built and tested in: Codex App
Model: GPT-5.4
Reasoning effort: Extra High
Testing: focused local test

target.title: # PR: Filesystem Access Control (PathGuard)
target.body:
# PR: Filesystem Access Control (PathGuard)

## Summary

This PR introduces a stricter, policy-driven filesystem access layer (**PathGuard**) for OpenClaw agent filesystem tools, including local media (image/pdf) loaders.

It closes key security and consistency gaps by:
- canonicalizing requested paths before evaluation (realpath-aware, ENOENT-safe),
- preventing traversal and symlink/junction escapes,
- enforcing `allowedPaths` / `denyPaths` consistently for classic filesystem tools **and** local media loads,
- preserving **deny-overrides-allow** semantics,
- anchoring workspace-relative policy entries to the workspace root (and re-anchoring after realpath),
- treating `allowedPaths: []` as an explicit **deny-all**,
- supporting absolute glob policy entries (via minimatch) alongside canonical absolute literals,
- returning structured, remediation-focused policy denial tool results (`policy_denied`) when access is blocked,
- and enforcing a monotonic filesystem policy ceiling for spawned subagents (global + agent + subagent defaults + spawn-time tightening), plumbed end-to-end into the spawned run.

**Important scope note:**

R: “This PR secures filesystem tools; it does not sandbox arbitrary shell execution.”

Remote URLs (`http(s)://`) and inline `data:` inputs are not treated as filesystem paths and are outside this layer.

---

## Change Type

- [x] Feature
- [x] Security hardening
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Docs
- [x] Tests

---

## Linked Issues

- Closes #39672
- Related #8719

---

## Problem Statement (What was wrong before)

Before this PR, filesystem tool enforcement had multiple gaps:

1) **Path canonicalization and symlink escape handling were fragmented**
- Traversal protections and “what path are we actually touching?” logic were spread across tools/flows.
- Non-existent paths (ENOENT) were tricky: naive realpath calls fail and can allow later-creation escapes.

2) **Policy matching was inconsistent**
- Absolute vs relative entries could be evaluated in different “path spaces”.
- Glob vs non-glob entries could diverge in behavior, especially when “roots” filtering was used as an approximation.

3) **Media tools could diverge from file tool policy**
- Local file references inside image/pdf flows could reopen outside-workspace reads if not enforced per resolved file.

4) **Sandbox and host flows lacked a unified enforcement story**
- Enforcement needed to be identical regardless of whether the run is sandboxed or host-based.

5) **Spawned subagents did not have a guaranteed filesystem policy ceiling**
- Subagents needed an explicit, monotonic ceiling that could not be loosened at spawn time.

---

## What Changed (Design + Implementation)

### 1) Core PathGuard enforcement (`src/security/path-guard.ts`)

PathGuard implements:

- **Canonical resolution for existing paths** via `fs.realpath`.
- **Nearest-existing-parent resolution** for ENOENT paths (prevents “create later via symlink” bypass).
- **Symlink/junction-aware comparisons** in canonical path space.
- **Deny precedence**: deny rules always override allow rules.
- **Workspace-only boundary**: `workspaceOnly` blocks outside-workspace access.
- **Relative entry anchoring**: workspace-relative policy entries are anchored to the workspace root, and re-anchored after realpath resolution.
- **Empty allowlists**: `allowedPaths: []` is treated as an explicit deny-all.
- **Absolute policy entries**:
  - absolute **literals** are canonicalized before comparison,
  - absolute **globs** are supported (matched against canonical real paths) without attempting to realpath the pattern.
- **Glob detection** via `Minimatch(...).hasMagic()` (brace/extglob supported).

### 2) Filesystem tool integration (read/write/edit/apply_patch-style)

- Tool FS config is resolved through the tool/fs policy configuration and enforced using `checkPathGuardStrict(...)`.
- Wrappers normalize args and run PathGuard checks on resolved paths.
- `apply_patch` is explicitly guarded by parsing patch hunks and enforcing FS policy on each patch target path (not just args.path/file_path).

### 3) Structured `policy_denied` tool result (model guidance)

When PathGuard denies access, tools return a structured tool result (instead of only throwing a raw error) that:
- states the restriction is system-enforced and cannot be bypassed,
- describes what the tool attempted to do,
- provides actionable remediation options,
- and explicitly points to config keys that can be changed to grant access.

This improves model behavior: fewer useless retries, more direct user remediation.

### 4) Media tool integration (image/pdf local paths)

Local media loads are now policy-checked on the resolved file path:
- `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts`
- `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.ts`

Key invariant:
- enforcement is per resolved path using `checkPathGuardStrict(...)`, not via root-prefix approximations.

### 5) Sandbox behavior

For local media loads in sandbox mode:
- PathGuard runs in sandbox flows too,
- policy root uses `sandbox.root` when sandboxed,
- otherwise `workspaceDir` is used.

### 6) Subagent filesystem policy ceiling (spawn-time tightening + runtime enforcement)

Goal: spawned subagents must never receive broader filesystem access than the configured ceiling.

Policy sources (monotonic tightening):
- Global: `tools.fs`
- Per-agent: `agents.<id>.tools.fs`
- Subagent defaults/ceiling: `tools.subagents.fs`
- Sessions-spawn defaults/ceiling: `tools.sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` (applied when the tool call omits `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`)
- Spawn-time tightening: `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`

Merge semantics:
- `workspaceOnly`: OR
- `denyPaths`: UNION
- `allowedPaths`: enforced as a ceiling/tightening model (empty list = deny all)

Persistence + plumbing:
- Effective policy is persisted on the spawned child session (`spawnedToolFsPolicy`) via `sessions.patch`.
- Gateway plumbs it into the child run as ingress field `toolFsPolicy`.
- Gateway session resets (`/new` / `/reset`) preserve `spawnedToolFsPolicy` (no widening after reset).
- Embedded runner passes it into tool construction.
- `createOpenClawCodingTools` accepts an `fsPolicy` override and uses it as the effective policy for that run.
- Nested spawns inherit the parent session’s `spawnedToolFsPolicy` ceiling before applying config/tool-call tightening.

---

## Configuration (for contributors)

### Filesystem policy knobs

- `tools.fs.workspaceOnly: boolean`
- `tools.fs.allowedPaths: string[] | undefined` (empty array means deny-all)
- `tools.fs.denyPaths: string[] | undefined`

Subagent ceiling:
- `tools.subagents.fs.{workspaceOnly, allowedPaths, denyPaths}`

Sessions-spawn defaults + spawn-time tightening:
- `tools.sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` (config default ceiling/tightening)
- `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` (tool arg tightening; can only further restrict)

Notes:
- Deny always wins.
- Relative entries are workspace-anchored.
- Policies are evaluated against canonicalized real paths.

---

## Explicit Non-Goals / Out of Scope

- Exec sandboxing is not implemented here.
  R: “This PR secures filesystem tools; it does not sandbox arbitrary shell execution.”
- No shell argument parsing.
- Remote source governance is out-of-scope.

---

## Implementation Notes (for contributors)

### Policy evaluation edge cases covered

- `allowedPaths: []` is treated as an explicit **deny-all** (not “no restriction”).
- Relative literal entries are **re-anchored after realpath**: if a workspace-relative entry canonicalizes outside the workspace (e.g. it points at a symlink to an external dir), it **does not** match outside-workspace targets.
- Absolute glob entries support symlink-alias authoring by **canonicalizing the non-glob prefix** before matching.
  - When rebuilding the rewritten pattern, the implementation **normalizes slash joining** so root-anchored globs stay semantically equivalent (e.g. `"/**/*.pem"` must not become `"//**/*.pem"`).

### Tool behavior on denial (model guidance)

When a filesystem access is blocked by PathGuard, tools return a structured `policy_denied` result (English text + structured fields) so models:
- do not attempt “bypass retries”,
- clearly communicate what was attempted,
- present actionable remediation options,
- and point to config keys (`tools.fs.*`) for operators to change if access is intended.

### Subagent filesystem ceiling (monotonic tightening)

Effective subagent policy is computed as a ceiling and is monotonic (cannot be widened by spawn calls):
- global: `tools.fs`
- agent: `agents.<id>.tools.fs`
- subagent defaults/ceiling: `tools.subagents.fs`
- sessions-spawn defaults: `tools.sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`
- spawn-time tightening: `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` / tool arg `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`

Merge intent:
- `workspaceOnly`: OR
- `denyPaths`: UNION
- `allowedPaths`: ceiling/tightening model (empty list = deny all)

The effective ceiling is persisted on the child session (`spawnedToolFsPolicy`) and forwarded into the embedded runner (`toolFsPolicy` → `createOpenClawCodingTools({ fsPolicy })`).

---

## Verification

- CI checks and tests pass (per latest runs).
- Added/maintained coverage ensuring `tools.sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` is applied as a default tightening when the tool call omits `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`.
- Verified critical denial scenarios: traversal, symlink/junction escapes, ENOENT parent-walk, deny precedence, empty allowlist deny-all, sandbox media enforcement, apply_patch enforcement, and subagent ceiling propagation.
- Verified monotonic nested spawning: a tightened subagent cannot spawn a child with broader FS access (parent `spawnedToolFsPolicy` is inherited).
- Verified gateway resets (`/new` / `/reset`) preserve the spawned FS ceiling (no widening after reset).

---

## Reviewer / Contributor Notes (Do not regress these invariants)

- Do not replace per-path enforcement with root-prefix approximations for glob policies.
- Keep deny-overrides-allow.
- Keep relative policy entries anchored to workspace (including after realpath).
- Keep sandbox and host local-file enforcement aligned.
- Keep local filesystem policy and remote-source policy separate concepts.
- Keep subagent policy tightening monotonic (no privilege escalation vs ceiling).
- Remember: exec is outside this enforcement layer.

---

## Rollback / Recovery

- Disable restrictions by setting `workspaceOnly: false` and clearing `allowedPaths` / `denyPaths`.
- No data migration required.
